messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — I captured a perf/flame run on a prod tail that showed surprising CPU time in Python/tokenize + scheduler wakeups. Uploading snippets below.

maria: perf command I ran: `sudo perf record -F 200 -p $(pidof redwood-runtime) -g -- sleep 60` then `perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded` -> flamegraph. Took ~60s sampling during a high-latency batch spike.

sanjay: Can you paste the top stacks (text) instead of svg so we can grep?

maria: Top collapsed stacks (percent samples):
- 12.3% python3 _PyEval_EvalFrameDefault -> tokenizer._fast_tokenize -> tokenize_inner
- 9.8% BatchScheduler::wake_if_needed -> futex_wait -> pthread_cond_signal
- 8.7% KVCache::lock_evict -> spin_lock -> futex_wake
- 6.5% PyObject_Call -> model_dispatch -> kernel_selector::choose_kernel
- 5.1% GIL.acquire -> tokenization threadpool submit

maria: So two signals: tokenizer in Python is ~12% and we have both scheduler wakeups (lots of short sleeps) and a small but hot KVCache eviction lock.

taylor: :thinking: Tokenizer overhead of ~12% matches flakiness we've seen for small prompt bursts. Are we running tokenization inline on the request thread?

maria: Yes. Current flow: request thread calls into python tokenizer, then enqueues tokens into batcher. Batcher has `max_batch_delay_ms=10, min_batch_size=1`. Code snippet: `if (queue_size==0) wait_for(timeout_ms=10) else flush_immediately()`

elaine: If we're waking every 10ms with min_size=1 we'll see a lot of wakeups during tails. What does perf show for futex/syscall rates?

maria: Sample shows many `futex_wait`/`futex_wake` pairs clustered in the same stacks as BatchScheduler::pop_batch. Roughly 3x more futex events in the bad run vs baseline. KVCache spinlock shows short critical sections but many repeated tries (~5-10 per request when cache misses spike).

sanjay: Two-pronged mitigation: (A) move tokenization off the request thread to a small worker pool (background) so request threads don't hit Python as much, (B) slightly increase max_batch_delay to reduce wakeups. Lower risk than touching kernel selection.

taylor: Also consider switching tokenizer to a Rust extension for hot paths — eliminates GIL time. But that's medium-term. Short-term worker pool + batching tweak seems safe.

maria: I validated quickly with a local service replay: bumping `max_batch_delay_ms -> 15` reduced futex events by ~30% and CPU p10 improved ~20ms. Background tokenization (threadpool size 4) pushed python self CPU from 12% -> 4% in the sample run.

perf-bot: nsys run 12345 finished: GPU kernel timelines show no major kernel queuing or memcpy stalls during the sampled window — GPU looks fine.

elaine: Good—so kernel selection regressions unlikely here. Still want to keep eye on `kernel_selector::choose_kernel` samples (6.5%). Might be expensive when model variant lookups happen per-request. Caching selector decisions could be a separate perf win.

sanjay: Action items:
- maria: open a small PR behind a feature flag with (1) tokenizer background pool, (2) bump max_batch_delay_ms=15, (3) add perf-test job to CI that runs 60s perf sampling on the replay.
- taylor: prototype a Rust tokenizer PoC for follow-up.
- elaine: add a light-weight KVCache contention metric (lock hold time histogram) to Console.

maria: I'll add the PR and attach the out.folded + a short howto to reproduce: `sudo perf record -F 200 -p $(pidof redwood-runtime) -g -- sleep 60; sudo perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded` and `./flamegraph.pl out.folded > perf.svg`. Also including the small perf text excerpt I pasted.

taylor: :thumbsup: For canary: enable flag on a single Dedicated shard during low-traffic window, run the synthetic long-tail replay, compare p50/p90/p99 and futex rate. If no regressions, we roll.

sanjay: Add a short note in the release changelog about tokenizer opt and batching flag so support can correlate customer reports.

maria: Will do. Thanks all — I'll link the PR here when ready. :eyes:
